name: M3CAD
description: We introduce M$^3$CAD, a novel benchmark designed to advance research in generic cooperative autonomous driving. M$^3$CAD comprises 204 sequences with 30k frames, spanning a diverse range of cooperative driving scenarios. Each sequence includes multiple vehicles and sensing modalities, e.g., LiDAR point clouds, RGB images, and GPS/IMU, supporting a variety of autonomous driving tasks, including object detection and tracking, mapping, motion forecasting, occupancy prediction, and path planning. This rich multimodal setup enables M$^3$CAD to support both single-vehicle and multi-vehicle autonomous driving research, significantly broadening the scope of research in the field. To our knowledge, M$^3$CAD is the most comprehensive benchmark specifically tailored for cooperative multi-task autonomous driving research. We evaluate the state-of-the-art end-to-end solution on M$^3$CAD to establish baseline performance. To foster cooperative autonomous driving research, we also propose E2EC, a simple yet effective framework for cooperative driving solution that leverages inter-vehicle shared information for improved path planning. We release M$^3$CAD, along with our baseline models and evaluation results, to support the development of robust cooperative autonomous driving systems. All resources will be made publicly available on https://github.com/zhumorui/M3CAD
evaluation_method: multiple_metrics (task-specific: mAP for detection, MOTA/MOTP for tracking, ADE/FDE for forecasting, IoU for occupancy, task_success_rate for planning)
general_score_metric: task-specific metrics (mAP, ADE/FDE, MOTA, IoU, task_success_rate)
reputation: Recently released academic benchmark focused on cooperative multi-vehicle tasks; early-stage but gaining attention in cooperative autonomous driving research.
notes: Multimodal, non-LLM benchmark; relatively small scale (204 sequences, ~30k frames) compared with large driving datasets; evaluation is task-dependent so no single unified metric; potential domain gap to diverse real-world driving conditions.
